data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The smallest positive integer satisfying x \u2261 3 (mod 5) and x \u2261 4 (mod 7) is 18, found by stepwise search along the residue chain 3, 8, 13, 18.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If a positive integer smaller than 18 satisfies both congruences, this candidate is overturned.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the progression 5k+3 has a positive term below 18 that leaves remainder 4 mod 7, the chain analysis is incomplete.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The constraints x = 5k + 3 (k \u2265 0) and x = 7m + 4 (m \u2265 0) generate the arithmetic progression {3, 8, 13, 18, ...}. The search walks this chain from its origin: x=3 leaves 3 mod 7 (not 4); x=8 leaves 1; x=13 leaves 6; x=18 leaves 4. At k=3, m=2, both congruences hold simultaneously. The progression increases by 5 each step and is bounded below by 3, so no positive integer smaller than 18 can lie on the 5-chain; among {3, 8, 13}, none satisfies the mod-7 test. Therefore 18 is the least positive solution and the complete solution is x \u2261 18 (mod 35).","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
